summary.title: Roll your own IRC bot
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a small IRC bot in Haskell, progressing from a raw socket connection to a reader-monad design with PING handling, commands, and an uptime feature.
keywords: write your own control structure haskell
takeaways: How to connect to an IRC server in Haskell using the network package and a socket Handle
How to send IRC commands (NICK, USER, JOIN, PRIVMSG) and respond to PING messages
How to hold read-only bot state in a ReaderT-based Net monad and use bracket for setup and teardown
How to add a simple command (uptime) by extending the bot state with a start time
summary.summary: This tutorial by Don Stewart walks through writing a small IRC bot in Haskell in incremental numbered files. It starts with connecting to irc.libera.chat over a socket, then adds joining a channel, sending and receiving protocol lines, and a simple eval-based command dispatcher for !id and !quit. It then refactors the bot into a ReaderT monad carrying the socket, uses bracket and liftIO, and finally adds an !uptime command with a custom time formatter. The page ends with suggestions for further hacking, such as adding a forkIO command line interface.
